DOCSIS Technology
Sep 28, 2026

Turning Up the Spectrum: DOCSIS 4.0 Technology Goes to 3 GHz

Share
FacebookLinkedInX

Key Points

Content
The new optional annex to the DOCSIS 4.0 Physical Layer Specification extends downstream operation to 3 GHz, giving cable operators a path to increase capacity over existing HFC networks.
The technology, developed in collaboration with operators and vendors, defines downstream requirements to 3 GHz for both Node/Remote PHY Device (RPD) equipment and cable modems — an industry first.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:12
Instaread

Broadband networks must continually evolve to support growing demand for faster speeds and greater capacity in today’s highly competitive environment. For cable operators, the challenge is finding new ways to meet that demand while continuing to leverage the extensive hybrid fiber coax (HFC) networks already serving millions of customers. To meet that challenge, CableLabs has developed a new optional annex to the DOCSIS® 4.0 Physical Layer Specification that extends downstream operation to 3 GHz — unlocking up to 25 Gbps of aggregate network capacity over existing HFC infrastructure.

Published this month, the annex is the product of close collaboration between cable operators, industry vendors and CableLabs — and marks an industry first: defining downstream requirements to 3 GHz for both Node/RPD equipment and cable modems.

Unlocking More Potential From HFC

The opportunity starts with the coaxial cable network already installed serving millions of homes worldwide. That cable is not simply a legacy asset — it is a vastly capable broadband medium with room for continued expansion and growth. Using more of its available spectrum gives operators a powerful new option for increasing downstream capacity without walking away from the networks they have spent decades building.

This expanded spectrum keeps capacity well ahead of bandwidth demand. Turning that latent potential into deployable technology requires industry alignment. Operators need confidence that equipment will interoperate and perform as expected, while vendors need a common set of requirements around which they can design products.

A CableLabs specification provides that foundation, transforming an ambitious idea into a practical, interoperable path for the next evolution of HFC networks.

Defining the Path to 3 GHz

At SCTE TechExpo25, CableLabs CEO Phil McKinney announced that CableLabs would begin work focused on enabling HFC networks to support DOCSIS data transmission up to 3 GHz and, longer term, 6 GHz. Now, a year later, that work has resulted in a completed specification — a rapid progression made possible by broad industry collaboration.

Last year, CableLabs brought together physical-layer experts from cable operators and equipment vendors in the DOCSIS 4.0 PHY Working Group, which was open to all interested participants. The effort began with presentations from industry experts showcasing the current state of technology in areas such as amplifier hybrids, optical Node/RPD silicon, cable modems, taps, passives, cables and connectors.

Using this information, the group developed cable plant models capable of supporting operation to 3 GHz. This analysis helped the working group determine what is technically feasible at frequencies up to 3 GHz with today’s technology.

After extensive technical discussions, the group agreed on how many orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) resources — each with a bandwidth of 192 MHz — should be supported by Node/RPD equipment and cable modems. The group extended the DOCSIS 4.0 Physical Layer Specification, establishing requirements where they remained applicable and augmenting them where operation at higher frequencies demanded additional detail. The work included requirements and guidelines addressing important performance areas such as Total Composite Power (TCP) and Carrier-to-Composite Noise (CCN). These requirements were carefully developed to provide meaningful guidance to equipment manufacturers and operators without unnecessarily constraining future industry innovation.

These additions establish performance expectations for both the Node/RPD and cable modem sides of the network, creating a common technical foundation for downstream operation to 3 GHz. Some areas will require continued research as implementations, test results and additional simulation data emerge. The technology will continue to evolve as the industry gains experience at higher frequencies and new capabilities become practical.

Join Us

This effort demonstrates what the cable industry can accomplish when operators, equipment manufacturers and technology experts work together. The resulting specification provides valuable guidance for operators considering the next stage of their network evolution while laying the groundwork for continued innovation toward 3 GHz and beyond. Join a working group to get involved!

If you’re attending SCTE TechExpo26 and want to dig deeper into DOCSIS 4.0 technology, join CableLabs for the DOCSIS 4.0 Meetup on Tuesday, Sept. 29, at 4:45–5:30 p.m. in the Connections Lounge. Join us for this interactive discussion on deployment strategies, operational readiness and what’s next for DOCSIS 4.0 networks.

Together, we can continue to build this new and exciting chapter for the industry!
